## Motivation

With `CUDA_MODULE_LOADING=EAGER` and `--tokenizer-worker-num > 1`, the HTTP/tokenizer workers never all come up. The server log prints `Waiting for child process [pid]` / `Child process [pid] died` every few seconds, indefinitely, and `ps` shows a single `sglang::tokenizer_worker` next to a queue of `spawn_main` processes at 100% CPU.

Cause:

- uvicorn starts the workers with the spawn context, so each worker re-imports `sglang`. Platform detection at import (`torch.cuda.is_available()`, plus the module-level `is_cuda()` checks) initializes CUDA in the worker.
- Under `EAGER`, that CUDA init loads every kernel module up front. We measured ~2 min of CPU and several GB of RSS per worker for `torch.cuda.is_available()` alone, against ~1–2 s with `LAZY`.
- uvicorn pings each worker with `timeout_worker_healthcheck` (`SGLANG_UVICORN_WORKER_HEALTHCHECK_TIMEOUT`, default 10 s), and the worker's pong thread only starts after the import finishes. Every fresh worker misses the healthcheck, is killed, and is respawned into the same state.

Raising `SGLANG_UVICORN_WORKER_HEALTHCHECK_TIMEOUT` hides the loop, but each worker still pays minutes of CPU and GBs of memory for a CUDA init it does not use.

## Modifications

- `http_server._use_lazy_cuda_module_loading_for_http_workers()`: if `CUDA_MODULE_LOADING` is `EAGER`, set it to `LAZY` in the parent's environment and log it. Called at the top of the multi-tokenizer branch of `_setup_and_run_http_server`, so it covers the uvicorn, SO_REUSEPORT and Granian multi-worker paths, plus workers that uvicorn later respawns.
- Scheduler processes are not affected. `launch_server` only reaches `_setup_and_run_http_server` after `Engine._launch_subprocesses` has returned, so the schedulers, detokenizer and DP controller are already running. They keep the environment they were spawned with, and CUDA reads `CUDA_MODULE_LOADING` at init in each process.
- No-op when `EAGER` is not set, with `--tokenizer-worker-num 1`, on the Rust server path, and on `node_rank >= 1`.
- Test: `test/registered/unit/entrypoints/test_http_server_worker_cuda_module_loading.py` (CPU). It checks the env mapping (`EAGER`/`eager` → `LAZY`, `LAZY` and unset unchanged), and that a spawn-context child sees `EAGER` before the call and `LAZY` after it.

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable: no kernel or model code changes.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable to serving throughput. With the change, workers start in seconds under `EAGER` instead of being killed in a loop.

## Testing

- `pre-commit run` on the changed files: passed.
- The helper's env mapping and spawn inheritance were checked in a standalone script.
- The new unit test has not been run locally (no torch environment on the authoring machine); CI runs it in `base-a-test-cpu`.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

+        "starting HTTP workers with CUDA_MODULE_LOADING=LAZY."

+"""HTTP/tokenizer workers must start with lazy CUDA module loading even when the
+server runs with CUDA_MODULE_LOADING=EAGER: a spawned worker initializes CUDA
+while importing sglang, and an eager init outlasts uvicorn's worker healthcheck.
+"""
+
+import multiprocessing
+import os
+import sys
+
+import pytest
+
+from sglang.srt.entrypoints import http_server
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cpu_ci
+
+register_cpu_ci(est_time=5, suite="base-a-test-cpu")
+
+
+def _report_cuda_module_loading(queue):
+    queue.put(os.environ.get("CUDA_MODULE_LOADING"))
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    "before, after",
+    [("EAGER", "LAZY"), ("eager", "LAZY"), ("LAZY", "LAZY"), (None, None)],
+)
+def test_http_workers_get_lazy_cuda_module_loading(monkeypatch, before, after):
+    if before is None:
+        monkeypatch.delenv("CUDA_MODULE_LOADING", raising=False)
+    else:
+        monkeypatch.setenv("CUDA_MODULE_LOADING", before)
+
+    http_server._use_lazy_cuda_module_loading_for_http_workers()
+
+    assert os.environ.get("CUDA_MODULE_LOADING") == after
+
+
+def test_spawned_worker_inherits_lazy(monkeypatch):
+    # uvicorn and granian start workers with the spawn context.
+    monkeypatch.setenv("CUDA_MODULE_LOADING", "EAGER")
+    ctx = multiprocessing.get_context("spawn")
+
+    queue = ctx.Queue()
+    proc = ctx.Process(target=_report_cuda_module_loading, args=(queue,))
+    proc.start()
+    assert queue.get(timeout=60) == "EAGER"
+    proc.join(timeout=60)
+
+    http_server._use_lazy_cuda_module_loading_for_http_workers()
+
+    proc = ctx.Process(target=_report_cuda_module_loading, args=(queue,))
+    proc.start()
+    assert queue.get(timeout=60) == "LAZY"
+    proc.join(timeout=60)
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    sys.exit(pytest.main([__file__, "-v"]))
